newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Drnovsek voted in as new PM.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Drnovsek voted in as new PM.

text.p: Slovenia's parliament voted on Thursday to back acting centre-left Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek to head a new government by 46 votes to 44, Slovenian television reported.
Liberal Democrat Drnovsek clinched the knife-edge victory following the defection of an opposition rightwinger which gave him a crucial one-vote margin.
"Before us is a very demanding path. We need to form a government, we need to ensure Slovenia's political stability," Drnovsek told parliament after the vote was announced.
The parliamentary vote ended two months of political deadlock after a November 10 general election produced a hung parliament.
Drnovsek's Liberal Democrats and their allies, including former communists, held 45 seats with an alliance of three rightwing parties holding the other 45 seats.
A breakthrough came on Wednesday when a member of the Christian Democrats defected from his party and said he would support Drnovsek to end the stalemate.
